systems.name: Coding Assistant: Context Engineering Under 300 ms
systems.headline: One keystroke. Spend context where it helps.
systems.discoverySection: Let Two Requirements Set the Problem
systems.description: Retrieve relevant repository code, choose a model by task, and validate suggestions before the developer sees them.
systems.question: Complete calculate_total(items) using the repository’s existing tax helper.
systems.scope: The explorer follows serving-time suggestions. It shows a prepared repository index; it does not implement indexing, model hosting or a live IDE.
systems.provenance: Architecture, requirements and boundaries are adapted from the named canonical Markdown. Scenario branches, identifiers and payloads are illustrative teaching examples, not executions or measured results. Source assumptions remain assumptions.

discovery.question: Cloud or local?
discovery.decision: Choose where inference runs and what private code can leave the environment.

discovery.question: Real-time as the user types?
discovery.answer: Yes. The source sets a target below 300 ms for autocomplete.
discovery.decision: Budget cache, context, model and validation work; treat the figures as a design target.

discovery.question: Which IDEs and languages?
discovery.answer: VS Code, IntelliJ and Visual Studio; mainstream languages.
discovery.decision: Keep the extension thin and use a shared, IDE-agnostic backend.

discovery.question: Whole repository or current file?
discovery.decision: Build a ranked context funnel and retrieve a small relevant slice.

discovery.question: Private models and on-prem for enterprise?
discovery.decision: Enforce repository permissions, secret masking and private deployment options from the start.

stages.title: Collect the permitted workspace context
stages.what: A developer types def calculate_total(items). The extension authenticates and collects the current function, imports, cursor and relevant workspace signals. Secrets are masked before any external prompt.
stages.why: Whole-repository understanding does not mean sending the entire repository.

checks.text: Respect repository permissions and the chosen cloud or private deployment.

stages.title: Check a repository-scoped cache
stages.what: The cache looks for a compatible completion in this repository revision and context. This request misses, so it needs retrieval.
stages.why: A hit can avoid embeddings, retrieval and generation work; stale private-code results must not cross scope.
stages.next: Next: Find the existing tax helper.

checks.text: Repository, revision and context compatibility are added cache-key constraints in this example.

stages.title: Find the existing tax helper
stages.what: Semantic code search uses the already-built repository index. It retrieves compute_gst() and its real signature rather than inventing a second tax helper.
stages.why: Retrieving conventions and existing functions improves reuse without putting the whole repository in the prompt.

checks.text: Retrieve only code the developer may access.
Indexing is background preparation, not a full repository rebuild on each keystroke.

stages.title: Narrow the final prompt
stages.what: The prompt builder ranks the current function and retrieved helper, adds the task template and drops unrelated history. It records the template version.
stages.why: Context is a funnel: every token must justify its latency and cost.
stages.next: Next: Generate a plausible but invalid call.

checks.text: Fit the model context limit and exclude masked secrets.

stages.title: Route by the task, then generate
stages.what: This is a multi-line completion and the budget permits it, so the router selects the medium model route. It generates a completion using compute_gst(subtotal).
stages.why: A large reasoning model is not needed for every keystroke.
stages.next: Next: Validate before the suggestion is shown.

checks.text: The route follows the task policy, not a claim that one model meets every latency target.

stages.title: Validate before the suggestion is shown
stages.what: Validation parses the code, checks formatting and security, and verifies that compute_gst exists with this signature. Only accepted output proceeds.
stages.why: Plausible code can still call an invented API.
stages.next: Next: Offer a suggestion the developer controls.

checks.text: Resolve referenced APIs against the real repository.
Run validation-quality suites beyond this illustrative example.

stages.title: Offer a suggestion the developer controls
stages.what: The IDE offers the validated completion. The developer may accept all, accept part or reject; that feedback informs personalisation.
stages.why: The assistant suggests code; the developer owns the edit.
stages.next: A compatible cached completion is validated and offered without retrieval or model inference.

checks.text: Measure time to first safe suggestion separately from total generation time.

stages.what: The symbol check cannot resolve calculate_gst_fast. Validation rejects the candidate and ends this attempt without displaying it.

scenarios.label: Developer lacks repository access
scenarios.outcome: The request is denied before context collection, cache lookup, retrieval or inference.

stages.title: Stop at the repository permission check
stages.what: The extension requests context from a repository this developer cannot access. Authentication succeeds but repository authorisation fails.
stages.why: An authenticated developer is not entitled to every repository.
stages.next: The request is denied before context collection, cache lookup, retrieval or inference.

checks.text: No private repository text is read or sent to a model.

revision.pitch: I would treat this as context engineering under a latency budget. The IDE sends the current task and a narrow, permission-scoped view of the workspace. We mask secrets and respect cloud or private deployment policy. A compatible scoped-cache hit can skip retrieval and inference. On a miss, semantic search finds relevant code and existing helpers from a background-built index. The prompt builder ranks those signals and fits the task template into the context window. The router uses a small route for simple completion and stronger routes for harder tasks. Before anything reaches the IDE, validation checks syntax, security and whether the referenced APIs actually exist. Invalid output is suppressed or regenerated within a bounded budget. The developer remains in control of the edit. The source’s 300 millisecond budget is a target to measure, not evidence that this explorer meets it.
revision.flow: Permitted context → scoped cache → retrieval on a miss → prompt funnel → task-based model route → validation → developer-controlled suggestion
requirements: Single- and multi-line completion, explanation, tests, docs, commit messages, refactoring, bug fixes, Q&A, code search, multiple languages and workspace awareness.
Autocomplete target below 300 ms, useful and accurate output, availability, enterprise security, personalisation, millions of developers and controlled cost.
discovery: Private models and on-prem for enterprise?
revision.tradeoff: More context may improve suggestions, but raises token cost and latency. Larger models buy reasoning only where the task needs it.
revision.failure: A model emits a helper that does not exist. Validate against repository symbols and suppress the candidate rather than presenting plausible code as working code.
ops: Stateless serving, repository-aware index sharding and nearby inference absorb keystroke demand. Background indexing is separate.
The source allocates roughly 10 ms cache, 40 ms context, 200 ms inference and 50 ms validation. These rounded figures total 300 ms and do not prove a below-300 ms result or include all overhead.
Cache compatible completions, keep prompts small and use the least costly model route that meets task quality.
Measure useful suggestion acceptance, nonexistent-API failures, privacy isolation and time to first validated suggestion.
revision.remember: More context is useful only when it earns its token and latency cost.
